title: The locus where the fibre dimension of a finite type ring map is at most d is a neighbourhood of a point where it equals d
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings of finite type [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. For a prime ideal $\mathfrak q'\subset S$ with $\mathfrak p'=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q')$, let $\kappa(\mathfrak p')$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q')$ be the residue fields, $F_{\mathfrak p'}=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p')$ the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], $\mathfrak Q'\subset F_{\mathfrak p'}$ the kernel of the ring map $F_{\mathfrak p'}\to\kappa(\mathfrak q')$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$ (a prime ideal), and let $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)$ be the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}F_{\mathfrak p'}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] at the point $\mathfrak Q'$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point]. Let $d\ge0$ be an integer and $\mathfrak q\subset S$ a prime ideal with $\dim_{\mathfrak q}(S/R)=d$. Then there is an open subset $V\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}S$ (Zariski topology) with $\mathfrak q\in V$ such that $\dim_{\mathfrak q'}(S/R)\le d$ for every prime $\mathfrak q'\in V$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00QH (lemma-dimension-fibres-bounded-open-upstairs, line 31308) and its proof (via Lemma Tag 00QE, lemma-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra, and Lemma Tag 00QG, lemma-dimension-quasi-finite-over-polynomial-algebra); dim_q(S/R) is Definition Tag 00QD (definition-relative-dimension, line 31150); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: Apply the existing Tag 00QE theorem at q with n = d to obtain g outside q, a polynomial R-algebra map f to S_g, its finite type proof and quasi-finiteness at every prime. The preimageEquivFiber point in the dimension hypothesis equals the preimageHomeomorphFiber point definitionally.

Take V = D(g), which is open and contains q. For every qprime in V, convert membership to g outside qprime and apply the polynomial-factorization fibre-dimension bound to g, d, f, the finite type proof and the quasi-finiteness hypothesis.
